name: build_work
description: Manage isolated broker work. Broker ID selects one independently deployable outcome: begin new work with a label and summary, omit to continue it, or reuse a returned ID. Broker Job ID identifies execution; Broker Release ID identifies publication. Session identity and request receipts are runtime owned. Ownership and publication gates remain enforced.

action.description: Arguments each action takes besides broker_id: begin label, summary (broker_id new); check check, expected_inputs_sha256, optional test_filter, feature_profile, timeout_seconds; preflight none (offset pages); finish expected_inputs_sha256; decide sync_decision, expected_sync_digest; status optional job_id; wait and cancel job_id; receipt request_id; review and reservations none; abandon none, or as an administrator task_key (task.id from takeover_preview) and reason to abandon any caller's task. Any other argument is refused by name.

task_id.description: Deprecated compatibility alias for broker_id. Do not supply both.

label.description: Required with begin: the new task's name and Broker ID, a lowercase hyphenated slug naming the outcome (e.g. abilities-chart-refresh). Unique; pick another if refused.

summary.description: Required with begin: one plain sentence describing the outcome, shown in full on the Broker card. No chat or session IDs; the runtime attaches them.

job_id.description: Broker Job ID. status inspects it; wait follows it again after an early still_running result (returning at the next alert or its end); wait without job_id but with broker_id follows that task's queued claim request until it is granted; cancel stops it and keeps the task for a fix.

feature_profile.description: check=check only: default compiles the linked build; live compiles the live host without linked implementation crates.

test_filter.description: check=test only: run just the tests whose names contain this text, such as a module path or test name.

broker_id.description: Omit to continue current broker work; new with begin (label and summary required) creates independent work; a returned Broker ID selects existing work. Runtime attaches chat identity. Never invent an ID.

examples: build and deploy my code change
run the checks on my source edits
release the change to the dev app
